headline: High: Plandex can write and execute against shared project files while Argo Workflows can ingest and act on those artifacts, creating default-path conflict and cascading-error risk.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: A has no browser or clipboard bridge, so direct prompt injection is not documented. B reads and writes project files and can execute shell, while A exposes REST/gRPC and produces artifacts/parameters; if A’s outputs are manually or file-fed into B, malicious content could steer B. The pathway is indirect, so low is appropriate.
conditions: IF A's artifacts are copied into B's project directory or stdin/stdout input
IF B parses A-generated files as instructions without a review step
mitigations: Keep A and B on separate directories
Require human review before B consumes any A output
Disable auto-apply in B for imported artifacts
Use a strict file allowlist for handoff files

B_data_leakage.rationale: A touches artifacts and parameters and has allowlisted network egress; B reads/writes the filesystem and sends data to a model provider or Plandex Cloud. If they share a workspace, B can ingest A-produced files and transmit their contents off-box. This is a default-path leakage risk, though not clearly irreversible.
conditions: IF A and B share the same project directory or mounted workspace
IF B uploads file contents from that workspace to its model provider or cloud backend
mitigations: Separate workspaces per agent
Block B from reading A output directories
Redact sensitive parameters before handoff
Use local-only model settings where available
Audit outbound requests for file payloads

C_capability_conflict.rationale: A can emit workflow artifacts while B can write the filesystem and modify git state; B also supports multiple instances via shared backend state. If both operate on the same repo or directory, concurrent writes and git mutations can clobber each other. The overlap is directly supported by both profiles, so high fits.
conditions: IF A and B target the same repository or working directory
IF B instances run concurrently while A is generating or updating artifacts
mitigations: Assign one writer per directory
Serialize git operations with a lock
Stage A outputs in a separate path
Disable concurrent B sessions on shared repos
Use branch-per-agent workflows

D_cascading_error.rationale: A produces artifacts and parameters that B can read from the filesystem and then act on with shell and git privileges. B’s review-then-apply mode helps, but auto-apply is optional and not disabled by default in the profile, so A’s output can become authoritative input for downstream actions. That creates a strong cascading-error pathway.
conditions: IF B ingests A-generated artifacts as task inputs
IF B auto-apply is enabled or human review is skipped
mitigations: Require verification before apply
Keep A outputs as read-only references
Turn off auto-apply
Add checksum or schema validation on handoff files
Limit B actions to dry-run mode for imported plans

E_compliance.rationale: No explicit residency, certification, or retention mismatch is documented for either agent. A is open-source Argo Workflows with docs-only evidence; B is Plandex with cloud or self-hosted backend options and model-provider calls. Because the compliance surface is underspecified, only a low-risk gap can be inferred, and uncertainty does not justify higher severity.
conditions: IF regulated data is routed through B's cloud or model-provider backend
IF A and B are deployed under different retention or residency policies
mitigations: Route regulated data only through approved backends
Document retention settings for both tools
Prefer self-hosted B for sensitive projects
Review vendor DPAs before use
